To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ALOX5 gene silencing protects heart cells against anoxia-reperfusion and ischemia-reperfuson injury in culture and in an animal model.
ALOX5 gene silencing by RNAi protects cardiomyocytes and the heart from ischemia-reperfusin injury.
ALOX5 gene silencing by RNAi protects cardiomyocytes against anoxia-reoxygenation and reduces the size of myocardial infarct in an open chest IR rat model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of myocardial infarct by means of gene silencing.
a new approach to cardioprotection based on the use of RNAi technology for silencing of ALOX 5 gene.
the possibility of using ALOX5 as a therapeutic target for RNAi-based treatment of heart IR injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the silencing of the gene encoding ALOX5 reduces the number of necrotized cardiomyocytes during anoxia-reoxygenation and ischemia-reperifusion.
ALOX5 downregulation by RNAi reduces the number of necrotized cardiomyocytes and the size of infarct zone during myocardial ischemia-reperusion injury.
ALOX5 downregulation by RNA interference is an effective cardioprotective strategy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
5-LOX gene silencing is an effective method of cardioprotection.
the ALOX5 is a good therapeutic target for RNAi application to protect against myocardial infarctions.
ALOX5 is a potential therapeutic target for myocardial IR injury and ALOX5 gene silencing may be a promising approach in the prevention of IR injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ALOX5 gene silencing protects myocardium against IR injury.
ALOX5 is a promising target for gene therapy in myocardial IR injury.
the ALOX5 gene is a potential target for the RNAi-based therapy of ischemic myocardial injury.
